correctness.rationale: Conditional on vertex barycentric coordinate T~Beta(1,d), every degree<=m multivariate polynomial has conditional polynomial q(T) of the same degree with q(1)=p(vertex). The positive-definite beta moment matrix provides the unique reproducing kernel k(T) and hence the sharp vertex L1 kernel norm. After s=dT, moment systems converge to the Exp(1) factorial Hankel matrix; coefficients converge to (-1)^m L_m/m!, and fixed-degree uniform integrability proves the limit. Independent sympy exact inversion for m=2,d=1,2,3,5 reproduced every stated quadratic coefficient and k(1)=binom(d+2,2)^2. Positivity defect is (V-1)/2 from integral 1. This is vertex, not global projector norm.
residual_risks: Independent checks are bounded, not proofs of universal statements.
